question: An uncomplicated monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancy with equal growth and normal Dopplers reaches 36 weeks. What is the recommended timing for elective delivery?

answers.text: 34 weeks, to avoid the risk of sudden intrauterine death from placental sharing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Delivery at 34 weeks is too early for an uncomplicated MCDA pregnancy and would carry significant neonatal prematurity morbidity. It is appropriate only if complications (TTTS, sIUGR) are present.

answers.text: 36–37 weeks, balancing the risk of stillbirth against prematurity morbidity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Current guidelines (RCOG, NICE) recommend delivery of uncomplicated MCDA twins at 36+0 to 37+0 weeks. The monochorionic placenta increases the risk of sudden cord-related or TTTS events, and this window minimises neonatal morbidity while avoiding late stillbirth.

answers.text: 38–39 weeks, the same as for singleton pregnancies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: DCDA twin pregnancies may be managed to 37–38 weeks, but MCDA twins require earlier delivery at 36–37 weeks because of the additional risks conferred by shared placental circulation.

answers.text: 40 weeks, only if the spontaneous onset of labour has not occurred

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Allowing an MCDA pregnancy to reach 40 weeks is not recommended. The risk of unexplained stillbirth in monochorionic twins rises significantly after 36–37 weeks due to the shared placenta.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the timing hierarchy: MCDA twins → 36–37 weeks; DCDA twins → 37–38 weeks; singletons → 39–40 weeks. Earlier delivery for higher shared-placenta risk.
Well done. 36–37 weeks is the evidence-based delivery window for uncomplicated MCDA twins, reflecting the higher risk of late intrauterine death compared to dichorionic pairs.
